free_tier.stated: 1 GB stored on the Spark (no-cost) plan; 10 GB/month downloaded (~360 MB/day)
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: Metered on Blaze at $1/GB, with 'No-cost up to 360 MB/day (equivalent to ~10 GB/month)' on Spark. 360 MB/day vs 500 GB/day = 1,400x short.

tooling: Firebase SDKs, REST API (`PUT/PATCH/GET .json`), Admin SDK, `firebase-tools` CLI; data is a JSON tree
chaining: 1 GB per database instance; multiple instances are possible via sharding, but the Spark plan limits you to a small number of instances and each shares the project's 10 GB/month download. 500 GB would need 500 projects.
limits_note: 1 GB stored; 10 MB max string (so ~7.5 MB of binary as base64); 256 MB max response per read; 32 levels max depth; 768 byte key length; 1,000 writes/sec per DB; 100 simultaneous connections on Spark; 10 GB/month download

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: Durable and simple, but base64 in JSON costs +33% and the 10 MB per-string cap means chunking into ~7.5 MB pieces. The 100-connection Spark limit and 360 MB/day download cap both bind hard.
confidence_note: Unverified: carried from historical research records without live verification. A first-party page read confirms documentation.
